#1677. Report: Liverpool face transfer dilemma that could change everything

Despite the transfer window slamming shut at the end of August, the rumour mill has never stopped turning.

Liverpool spent over £150 million on new players in the summer and, even though all four of them have had a solid impact on the Reds since they were brought in, it's clear that many issues are still plaguing Andoni Iraola's squad.

Right now, they're fourth in the Premier League and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

And, even though Iraola is doing everything he can to get his men back on track, nothing would help them more than adding a couple of new players to their ranks.

The January transfer window is now just around the corner which is where Liverpool will be given their best chance to improve things and get them back to the top of the Premier League table but, before that can happen, some tough decisions will need to be made.

Liverpool must figure out if they want to keep Virgil van Dijk or use one of their wonderkids

Virgil van Dijk's contract is set to expire in June 2027.

The towering Dutchman is still one of Liverpool's most important players and, without him, Liverpool would be nowhere near as good as they are.

Van Dijk may be 35 years old but, the fact that he's still an elite-level player proves how good he actually is.

In fact, Jeremy Jacquet has even claimed that he's lucky to be able to play alongside the Liverpool captain.

But, thanks to his age, some questions have arisen about whether he can continue performing to this level for much longer.

This has led to new centre-backs being linked with Liverpool as potential replacements.

No deals have been made just yet but, a new update from The Athletic has just given fans a good idea about how far off Liverpool believe the other centre-backs among their ranks are from their captain.

"Jeremy Jacquet has enjoyed an excellent start to his Anfield career, but the 21-year-old Frenchman has admitted he feels fortunate to be playing alongside Van Dijk," they wrote.

"There are high hopes for young centre-backs Giovanni Leoni (19 years old), Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye (both 18), but they are still learning their trade.

"With Joe Gomez also out of contract next summer and a decision to be made over whether Liverpool trigger their €55million (£46m; $61m) option to buy loanee Ronald Araujo from Barcelona, it is hard to envisage a scenario where waving goodbye to Van Dijk next May would make any possible sense. He is still unequivocally elite."

Liverpool must figure out their plans for the next few years

Right now, Iraola seems to be locked in with Liverpool for the long-run.

The Spaniard has done a fairly decent job at Anfield since taking over from Arne Slot so, at least the Reds are sorted in that department.

However, within their first-team squad, many different question marks are hanging over the heads of certain players.

These questions are making it hard for Iraola and Julian Ward to future-proof their squad which is why it's essential for decisions such as the future of Van Dijk to be confirmed as soon as possible.

If they don't manage to do this and leave things until April again as they did when Van Dijk's contract was last set to expire, they'll just be making things harder for themselves.

And, since they look unlikely to win the Premier League title this season, that'll almost certainly be their main goal next term.

So, for them to do this, they need a smooth transitional period and a clear idea of what moves they want to make in the summer.

Without this, they could end up doing even worse than they currently are and end up missing out on extending the stay of Van Dijk at Anfield.

#1676. Next Man United manager: "Serious coach" Mauricio Pochettino can be a huge success at Man United

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 14:23

As Manchester United close in on the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses the Argentine's suitability for the role with the 20-time English champions.

It looks like Pochettino. But there are strong indications that the USA want him to remain in charge for the two games against Haiti, on November 14 and November 17.

United go to Liverpool on the 22nd in the Premier League, straight after the international break. So it's very interesting to see what happens now.

I did see a report yesterday suggesting that Darren Fletcher may have another caretaker spell in charge just to take training. The players that are on international duty will return next week to prepare for that Liverpool game.

If Pochettino is not there until after the second game against Haiti, he will have limited preparation time for that Liverpool game.

So it'll be very interesting to see who takes training tomorrow, who takes it when the players are back in on Monday, and how that develops.

Pochettino is a very interesting name, one that wasn't particularly in the forefront. I think interestingly, the people behind the scenes at United couldn't agree on Conte, Eddie Howe or Nagelsmann, whether they were quite right at this stage.

I know Unai Emery is going to be signing a new deal with Villa, so that was always a no-go. Pochettino has gone from underdog with the bookies to the red-hot favourite. Personal terms are agreed. The compensation fee is around about £7.4m.

Then there is an extra, I think, about $2m for the staff that he will want to bring with him, the ones that have been with him throughout his time in management.

For me, I've always admired Pochettino. He's always wanted the United job. He's been linked with it numerous times before. He's always had a feeling that he could do a good job at Manchester United. His record is good. He finished sixth at Chelsea.

He won the league with PSG and finished second. Tottenham was really good, with a Champions League final, a second-place finish and then third a couple of times.

At Southampton, the eighth place finish he had when he first came to English football was really good. His brand of football was also really good, and so was his way of developing young players and getting them playing for him.

He's a serious coach. I think a lot of the criticism aimed at Carrick was almost like the boys' club mentality of "he's our mate, so he won't throw us under the bus".

That is great, and I do appreciate that. But Pochettino is a strong-minded individual who won't be afraid to tell people how it is. He has been in big dressing rooms. He's managed big players. He won't be overawed by the size of the task.

He'll know it's a big job. You get the feeling that he'll relish that challenge. He's not a young manager that's come in to prove his worth. He's 54. He's been around the block. He knows how it works. He's won big titles, and he's been in big games, so he knows exactly what's required.

His win rate at Tottenham was 54%. At PSG it was 65%. At Chelsea it was around about 51%. So he had his issues at Chelsea, and I know a lot of Chelsea fans are critical of him.

But Chelsea has been, for a while now, a difficult club to manage. So he had his problems there, but he also did a lot of good things at Chelsea. It was a really short spell at Stamford Bridge, 51 games.

Ultimately he'll be keen to show that he can still operate at this level. He signed a new deal with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup.

So it's a disappointment for them because I think they're going places. They've got some good young players and a good brand of football there.

But he was never going to turn down the chance to manage Manchester United. It feels like it's been a long time coming with him.

There is always a hint of optimism, but guarded optimism is probably the right phrase, just because it's so difficult to know.

History will tell you, certainly recent history, that it will ultimately probably go wrong at Manchester United. So guarded optimism would be the phrase I'd use at this stage.

I'm looking forward to what it could bring, getting in place for the Liverpool game. The interesting thing for me is the next few days. How does that develop? Do we get Fletcher in to take training on an interim? It's a strange one while they wait for Pochettino.

Bar a huge shock, he will be the next Manchester United manager. All guns ahead, all looking forward to that Liverpool game, which is a nice easy one to get going.

#1669. Opinion: Liverpool handed surprise chance to sign perfect Milos Kerkez successor

Milos Kerkez has been one of Liverpool's biggest disappointments over the last couple of years.

The Hungarian was brought in to replace Andy Robertson last season.

However, by the end of the campaign, the Scotsman managed to make himself Liverpool's first-choice left-back once again.

But, by the time the Reds realised that they needed him, he's already agreed a new deal with Tottenham.

This thrusted Kerkez into becoming the Reds' undeniable first-choice left-back with Kostas Tsimikas serving as his back-up.

Most people thought this added responsibility would help Kerkez but, if anything, he's managed to get worse.

This lack of form has been noticed by fans and pundits alike with the perfect option to replace him now emerging for Liverpool.

Rayan Ait-Nouri now wants to leave Manchester City

Ever since it was made clear that Kerkez's form wasn't going to improve, rumours have been circling about the next left-back that Liverpool could target.

Several different options have popped up recently with Brentford left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf seemingly on top of Iraola's shortlist.

However, since he's only just joined the Bees, a deal for the Senegal international feels highly unlikely to get over the line.

And, he's also had quite a slow start to life with Keith Andrews' men which is likely to have caused a worrisome thought or two.

But, since the footballing world is forever changing, new targets can emerge and, luckily for Liverpool, that seems to be exactly what has happened for them.

"Rayan Aït-Nouri could be a key player in the upcoming winter transfer window. The Algerian left-back is seriously considering leaving Manchester City and even wants to force a move as early as January," Sky Sports CH wrote.

"Two Italian clubs have already expressed interest: Juventus and Napoli. Contacts are underway between the player's representatives and the management of both clubs, who have now added Aït-Nouri to their shortlist to strengthen their left flank.

"The challenge now is to find the right formula to convince Manchester City. While the Citizens would ideally prefer a permanent transfer, this option appears financially difficult to realize this winter. Both Juventus and Napoli may lack the funds to meet the demands of a straight transfer.

"Under these conditions, the most likely scenario would be a paid loan with a purchase option, which could become mandatory under certain conditions."

Rayan Ait-Nouri would fit perfectly into Andoni Iraola's Liverpool plans

One of the best things about Ait-Nouri is that he can attack and defend.

Recently, it's felt like most left-backs have only been able to do one or the other.

For example, even though Kerkez has become Liverpool's first-choice left back, his defensive work has mostly been him recovering the ball thanks to his lightning-quick speed.

However, if he didn't have that, he would have ended up in a rather terrible situation on several occasions this term.

Ait-Nouri on the other hand, can attack and defend equally as well.

He's also got plenty of Premier League experience under his belt and has even chipped in with two assists for his teammates during his limited playing time this season.

Right now, a deal for any player to join Liverpool isn't all that likely but, if Iraola and Julian Ward are wanting to sign a new left-back, Ait-Nouri could be exactly what they're looking for.

#1663. Opinion: Liverpool loan transfer agreement now imminent for the next Harry Kane

There's a new Harry Kane, and a transfer for him is imminent at Liverpool.

There are plenty of brilliant strikers in world football right now, but surely nobody is operating at the same level as the current Ballon d'Or winner.

Kane is simply a phenomenal footballer. He's always been a ruthless goalscorer, but what makes Kane so special is that he's so much more than your traditional no.9.

His link-up play is exceptional. He can drop deep, dictate the tempo, pick out passes that most midfielders wouldn't even attempt and then somehow still find himself in the perfect position to score.

At Bayern Munich, Kane has taken his game to another level. His movement, intelligence and finishing ability make him an absolute nightmare for defenders.

And the frightening thing is that he doesn't rely on pace. His game is built around intelligence, technique and an extraordinary understanding of space.

There are younger, quicker strikers around, but very few can influence games in quite so many ways.

Why Liverpool need another no.9 soonLiverpool might have Alexander Isak scoring goals right now, and Hugo Ekitike is edging closer to his return from injury, but that doesn't necessarily mean the Reds are sorted in the striker department. Far from it. Isak is undoubtedly a world-class player on his day. However, his injury record remains a concern, and Liverpool simply cannot afford to rely on him staying fit throughout an entire season. Meanwhile, Ekitike is coming back from a devastating Achilles injury. There's no guarantee he'll immediately return to his best, and Liverpool will need to manage his minutes carefully. Looking at the bigger picture, the Reds need more depth and competition in attack. Andoni Iraola's demanding system requires forwards who can press relentlessly, stretch defences and maintain intensity throughout matches. Having just two recognised senior strikers isn't ideal. Ultimately, if Liverpool want to compete on multiple fronts, bringing in another exciting young no.9 makes perfect sense.

#1661. Forest Green apologise for failing to commemorate Remembrance Day at a home match due to 'mistake'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 10:15 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 07:03 EST, 9 November 2026

Forest Green Rovers have apologised for failing to commemorate Remembrance Day at a home game, labelling it as 'human error' and a 'mistake' from the club.

Remembrance Day is November 11 with Forest Green's sole fixture around that date having been Saturday's 2-0 FA Cup first-round defeat at Luton Town. Both teams commemorated the occasion ahead of kick-off at Kenilworth Road.

Forest Green's last home fixture prior to that was a 2-2 draw with Harrogate Town on October 31 in the National League.

That encounter at The New Lawn saw supporters of the fifth-tier side take to a fan forum post-match questioning why nothing was in place for Remembrance Day - due to their then-forthcoming clash with Luton being an away tie.

Forest Green CEO Dane Vince replied on the club's Fan Advisory Board, admitting it was an oversight on their part.

'The lack of Remembrance at a home game is simply down to a human error/mistake on the club,' he wrote.

Forest Green Rovers have apologised for not commemorating Remembrance Day at a home game (National League side pictured doing so during Saturday's FA Cup 2-0 defeat at Luton)

Forest Green failed to do so in their home draw vs Harrogate on October 31, calling it a 'mistake'

Vince continued that a condensed schedule in this period didn't help matters, but still acknowledged that the club should have done more.

'It didn't help that we had a sizable number of games in a small time frame (including the FA Cup replay) beforehand; albeit that isn't an excuse, we should have got this right.'

Following the incident, Vince confirmed that Forest Green would contact the Royal British Legion for advice on future commemorations to ensure this wouldn't happen again. He also underlined that the missed home commemoration did not signal any change in the club's support for Remembrance or the Royal British Legion.

'This was a simple error/mistake,' he reiterated.

#1660. Michael Carrick: Man United's shortest manager reigns ever after 45-year-old's sacking

By Joshua Cole | 12 Nov 2026 15:02

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign, bringing an abrupt end to the Englishman's second spell in charge at Old Trafford less than 10 months after he was appointed.

The 44-year-old initially arrived in January 2026 as a temporary replacement for Ruben Amorim, with the former midfielder making an immediate impression by restoring some confidence and guiding the Red Devils back into the Champions League picture.

Having overseen an encouraging improvement in results, Carrick was rewarded with a permanent contract in May, but his fortunes changed dramatically during the opening months of the new season.

United's disappointing results, inconsistent performances and growing concerns about their tactical direction ultimately proved too much for the club's hierarchy, with Sunday's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa preceding Man United's decision to relieve Carrick of his duties.

His departure adds another name to Manchester United's increasingly lengthy list of managerial casualties since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, although several managers in the club's history have endured even shorter spells in charge.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five of Manchester United's shortest managerial reigns, examining their appointments, records and the circumstances surrounding their departures.

Clarence 'Lal' Hilditch holds the distinction of having one of the shortest managerial spells in Manchester United's history, taking charge in October 1926 following the Football Association's suspension of John Chapman.

The former half-back became United's first player-manager, assuming responsibility for team affairs while continuing to feature on the pitch, but his appointment was never intended to be a long-term arrangement.

Hilditch oversaw 31 matches, winning nine, drawing eight and losing 14, giving him a win percentage of just 29.0%, with United struggling to establish consistency during his brief spell.

His final match came in April 1927, when United played out a goalless draw against Everton, before Herbert Bamlett was appointed as his replacement.

Although Hilditch's six-month spell was largely unsuccessful, he continued playing for the club until 1932, having made more than 100 appearances during his time at Old Trafford.

Walter Crickmer's first spell in charge of Manchester United lasted from November 1931 until the summer of 1932, when the club secretary temporarily assumed managerial responsibilities following the dismissal of Herbert Bamlett.

United had suffered relegation from the First Division in the previous campaign, having lost their opening 12 league matches and finished bottom of the table, leaving Crickmer with the difficult task of restoring some stability.

He managed 43 matches, winning 17, drawing nine and losing 17, which represented a win percentage of approximately 39.5%, as United recovered sufficiently to finish 12th in the Second Division.

Crickmer's time in the dugout ended when Scott Duncan was appointed as the club's new permanent manager in the summer of 1932, allowing him to return to his administrative responsibilities.

His departure was not the result of a dismissal, as Crickmer had primarily been acting as secretary-manager during a difficult period, and he would later take charge again between 1937 and 1945.

David Moyes remains one of the most prominent names on this list, having been selected by Ferguson to succeed him following his retirement in 2013.

The Scot officially took charge in July 2013, inheriting a team that had won the Premier League title by 11 points during Ferguson's final season, but quickly discovered that replicating his predecessor's success would be an enormous challenge.

Moyes began positively by winning the Community Shield against Wigan Athletic, before overseeing an impressive 4-1 Premier League victory against Swansea City in his first league match.

However, United's performances deteriorated as the campaign progressed, with defeats against Manchester City, Liverpool and Newcastle United exposing their difficulties against established Premier League opposition.

The Red Devils also suffered an embarrassing Champions League exit against Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals, while a 2-0 defeat against Everton in April 2014 proved to be Moyes's final match.

He departed on April 22, 2014, having won 27 of his 51 matches in charge, drawn nine and lost 15, giving him a win percentage of 52.9%.

Although Moyes had won the Community Shield, United were seventh in the Premier League and had already missed out on Champions League qualification, prompting the club to end his reign with four matches remaining.

Carrick's second spell at Old Trafford has now ended in disappointment, despite the considerable promise he demonstrated during his initial months in charge.

Appointed on January 13, 2026, following Amorim's dismissal, the former Middlesbrough manager quickly transformed United's fortunes, winning 11 of his first 16 Premier League matches and securing Champions League qualification.

His impressive work earned him a permanent position in May, with the club believing that his understanding of Manchester United's traditions and ability to establish a positive dressing-room atmosphere made him the right candidate for a longer-term project.

However, the challenges of managing United over a full campaign proved considerably more difficult, with his team collecting just three victories in their opening 15 matches of 2026-27.

Defeats against Bournemouth and Chelsea, alongside an embarrassing Champions League loss to Como, intensified scrutiny of his tactical approach, while a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa ultimately preceded his dismissal on November 12.

Carrick leaves with 15 wins, eight draws and nine defeats from 32 matches, representing a 46.9% win rate, although his initial success means his overall record is considerably better than his performances this season suggest.

Ruben Amorim's departure in January 2026 represented another significant managerial setback for Manchester United, with the Portuguese lasting just 14 months after replacing Erik ten Hag in November 2024.

United paid approximately £9.2m to release the former Sporting Lisbon manager from his contract, having been attracted by his impressive work in Portugal and his reputation for developing an organised, attack-minded team.

However, his preferred 3-4-3 system proved difficult to implement consistently at Old Trafford, with United struggling to produce convincing performances and suffering several damaging defeats during his first campaign.

The 2024-25 season ended with the club finishing 15th in the Premier League, their lowest position in the competition, while a 1-0 defeat against Tottenham Hotspur in the Europa League final denied them a route back into the Champions League.

Although there were occasional signs of improvement during the following campaign, disagreements over the club's footballing direction and continued inconsistency eventually undermined his position.

Amorim was dismissed on January 5, 2026, having recorded 24 victories, 18 draws and 21 defeats from 63 matches, giving him a disappointing win percentage of 38.1%.

His reign remains one of the least successful permanent managerial appointments of the post-Ferguson era, with Carrick now becoming the latest head coach to discover how difficult it is to restore Manchester United to their former standing.

#1656. Bonera believes Milan Futuro were not ready for first season: “Some thought it was easier”

Daniele Bonera has revisited his time as the head coach of Milan Futuro, revealing his belief that the team wasn’t ready to compete.

The Futuro project was launched ahead of the 2024-25 season to give Milan a ‘second team’ to allow their young talents to develop at a level above that of the Primavera league. They started in Serie C but were relegated in their first season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was taken to sack Bonera as the head coach given the on-field issues, even though they were competing against experienced sides with a very young side. Massimo Oddo followed him, before the club chose to go with Sergio Navarro this summer, who has the Futuro in third.

Bonera was interviewed by Fanpage and he reflected on that period with the B-team and what he learned from it even despite the rough results, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan Futuro was a great opportunity for growth. Perhaps we weren’t clear – and I’m part of this – about the level of Serie C. I had an idea of ​​it, but some thought it was easier,” he said.

“The squad had been built with expectations that were too high compared to what the league is. I don’t think that structure, at that time, was ready to tackle that type of league. On an individual level, however, I felt very comfortable. Starting at home was a positive thing.

“The biggest challenge was understanding which players you actually had available. Some were promoted to the first team, others were dropped, and still others were sent to the Primavera. We had guys who perhaps weren’t playing with us and then came back up.

“From an individual growth perspective, we worked very well in some situations. After a couple of years, we saw the individual value of guys like Camarda, Bartesaghi, Liberali, and Jimenez grow. The value of the players wasn’t in question.

“I think the problem was primarily structural: it’s not always the coach who’s the problem, but the way you do things and the direction you want to take.”

#1655. Opinion: One of the best young players in the world is coming to Liverpool

Whether in January or in the summer one of the best young players in the world is going to be heading to Liverpool.

Julian Ward has an enormous task on his hands at Liverpool, but there's also a genuine sense of excitement about what he's trying to build at Anfield.

The Reds are clearly looking towards the future. Ward wants to assemble a squad capable of dominating English and European football for years to come.

Essentially, he's trying to build Liverpool's next super team.

And when you look at some of the young players already at the club, there's plenty of reason to be optimistic.

Rio Ngumoha looks like a generational talent. Trey Nyoni is developing into an outstanding midfielder, while the likes of Florian Wirtz, Jeremy Jacquet and Bradley Barcola could become cornerstones of the team for the next decade.

Behind them, Liverpool have an academy packed with exciting prospects who could eventually make the step up.

Why Julian Ward needs time to achieve success with LiverpoolLiverpool supporters will understandably want immediate success, especially after watching the club struggle over the last few seasons. However, rebuilding a team isn't straightforward. There are still glaring weaknesses in the squad. Liverpool need a specialist holding midfielder, a natural right-winger and greater defensive depth. Questions also remain over the long-term futures of several experienced players. Ward cannot solve every problem in a single transfer window. Nor can Andoni Iraola be expected to transform this young squad into Premier League and Champions League winners overnight. These things take time. Just look at how Jurgen Klopp gradually assembled his great Liverpool side. It required several transfer windows, difficult decisions and plenty of patience before everything finally clicked. Liverpool have found their next Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, and he's incredible.

Liverpool are entering a new era under Julian Ward, and it's becoming increasingly clear that the club's transfer strategy is undergoing a significant transformation.

For years, the Reds built their success around identifying undervalued players who were ready to make an immediate impact.

Think Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane, Andy Robertson and Georginio Wijnaldum. Players who arrived at Anfield with something to prove and developed into world-class stars.

But now, Ward appears determined to take things in a slightly different direction.

Rather than waiting for players to establish themselves at the highest level, Liverpool want to identify the next generation of superstars before they become household names.

And it's an approach that makes a lot of sense.

How Liverpool are building a team for the futureThe transfer market has become increasingly expensive. Even relatively unproven players are commanding enormous fees, and Liverpool simply cannot afford to compete financially with the likes of Manchester City and Real Madrid for every established superstar. Instead, the Reds are looking to get ahead of the competition. We've already seen the club become far more aggressive in recruiting young talent from across the world. The arrivals of Mor Talla Ndiaye, Ifeanyi Ndukwe, Samuel Martinez, Armin Pecsi and Lucca Brughmans are all examples of Liverpool investing in players with enormous potential. Meanwhile, the club's academy is already producing exciting talents like Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni, Joshua Abe and Will Wright. The objective is simple. Liverpool want to build a conveyor belt of talent capable of sustaining success for the next decade.

#1648. Norway vs Wales - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 15:18, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:22

Two teams still in with a chance of making the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will lock horns on Saturday, with Norway hosting Wales.

Norway have actually lost each of their last three matches in Group A4 to give themselves a mountain to climb, while Wales have been beaten in three of their four games in the competition, but qualification for the final four is still possible at this stage.

Norway have a record of one win and three defeats from their four matches in Group A4, with three points leaving them at the bottom of the section on three points.

The Red, White and Blues are fourth but are level on points with third-placed Wales and only three points behind second-placed Denmark, so it is still all to play for ahead of the final two matchdays in the group stage.

Stale Solbakken's side opened their Group A4 campaign with a 3-2 success over Denmark, but they have lost twice to Portugal and also to Wales in their last three games.

Norway need to beat both Wales and Denmark, and a victory over the latter would be especially important, as they would then lead the head-to-head tie-breaker, which could potentially be crucial when it comes to the final positions in the section.

National Team are competing in League A of the Nations League for the first time, so they are bidding to secure what would be a first-ever quarter-final position.

Wales' route into the quarter-finals of the tournament is more complicated given that they have lost both games against Denmark, who therefore have the advantage in any head-to-head tiebreaker, which might be crucial after all of the fixtures have taken place.

Craig Bellamy's side had a difficult start to their Group A4 campaign, suffering back-to-back defeats to Portugal and Denmark at the end of September.

The Dragons then managed to post a 2-1 victory over Norway in their opening match of October, but they suffered a 1-0 loss to Denmark last time out.

Wales could join Denmark on six points with a win in this game, depending on what occurs between the Danes and Portugal, which would put them in a position to claim a top-two spot, but so much could still happen before the end of the section.

The Dragons have faced Norway on 12 occasions, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and four defeats, and they have actually been victorious in each of the last three matches between the two sides.

Norway have four players who are one booking away from missing the team's next match, including Martin Odegaard.

There are not expected to be any major surprises in the Norway side for this match, with Oscar Bobb and Antonio Nusa both expected to feature in the final third of the field.

Erling Haaland, meanwhile, is in line to win his 60th cap, and the striker will be looking to add to the 65 goals that he has scored for his country.

As for Wales, Benjamin Cabango and Sorba Thomas are both out of the match through suspension, while six other players are one booking away from being banned for the team's next fixture, including Ethan Ampadu.

Harry Wilson missed the team's last international period through injury, but the 29-year-old is available here and is set to start, while Daniel James could have a role through the middle against Norway.

Chris Mepham and Rubin Colwill are also potentially in line for starts on Saturday.

Norway have struggled in the section so far, but we are expecting Haaland to help the hosts secure a vital three points on Saturday.

The German headed back to Werder Bremen in the summer, and has been in remarkable form since. He has scored nine goals in the Bundesliga which makes him the top scorer, and 13 goals in 11 games across all competitions, at an average of one every 64 minutes.

#1643. Chelsea transfer news: Every Blues loan player ranked in minutes, quartet with less game time than Alejandro Garnacho

By Darren Plant | 12 Nov 2026 15:34, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:35

When Chelsea were searching for loan destinations for a wide array of their fringe players and starlets during the summer transfer window, they found themselves undertaking an elaborate operation.

With 24 players going elsewhere on a temporary basis, it was inevitable that some deals would bring less success than others.

Remarkably, five of the players who have recently departed Stamford Bridge are yet to reach 100 minutes for their respective clubs.

In sharp contrast, two teenagers have accumulated over 1,000 minutes, emphasising the different experiences that the players in question are having.

Here, Sports Mole reveals the amount of minutes that each of their loan players have racked up between the start of the campaign and the November international break.

Chelsea chiefs are being rewarded for finding suitable EFL clubs for a number of their academy players.

Most notably, 17-year-old winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has reached 718 minutes across 14 games for Championship club Portsmouth.

With the teenager also starring in a well-performing side, there are encouraging signs that he can become a future Chelsea first-teamer.

The same applies to central midfielder Reggie Walsh, who has amassed 923 minutes across 14 games for League One outfit Wigan Athletic.

Left-back Ishe Samuels-Smith is also up to 803 minutes across 12 games for Notts County, finally kick-starting his career after a frustrating period at Swansea City in 2025-26.

Defender Kaiden Wilson sits at the top of Chelsea loan players minutes list with 1,431 minutes over 18 appearances for League Two team Rochdale.

Much is being made of Alejandro Garnacho's situation at Aston Villa, and rightly so. The Argentine has racked up just 95 minutes across seven substitute outings.

However, there are four players - Shim Mheuka, Dujuan Richards, Landon Emenalo and Mykhaylo Mudryk - who have played even less minutes than Garnacho.

Chelsea will be frustrated that Mheuka and Emenalo are not getting more chances at Celtic. Despite their general inconsistency, Mheuka is yet to make a single senior start for the Glasgow giants.

There is an argument that as many as 15 players will be satisfied with their current situations out on loan.

Mamadou Sarr's time at Real Sociedad is going under the radar, with the Senegal international now up to 778 minutes across 10 games for the Spanish club.

Dario Essugo is also impressing at Strasbourg, contributing two goals and one assist from his 458 minutes in central midfield.

However, Jesse Derry is a clear example of someone who may be recalled in January, providing that the agreement with Sporting Lisbon include a break clause.

Derry has accumulated just 133 minutes across seven games for the Portuguese giants. Chelsea may look to find a suitable Championship club for the second half of the campaign, which would free up a foreign loan spot in the process.

#1641. Xabi Alonso was brought in to end the chaos at Chelsea and he is failing. PLUS: Football's most vanilla pundit gives out-of-his-depth Michael Carrick an easy ride: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

Published: 07:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:55 EST, 9 November 2026

The whiff of Premier League failure is in the air as the smoke clears from Bonfire Night.

It always feels this way by the time we get to the November international break.

Managers and their players have had time to settle in and teething problems no longer cut it as a reason for autumn struggles.

Worst of all, Christmas is coming and we all know what tends to happen to teams who are struggling as the end of the year nears.

So at places like Manchester United, Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Newcastle and Spurs there is anxiety about expectations not being met.

Xabi Alonso was hired to break the cycle at Chelsea and he is not yet succeeding

Xabi Alonso's side would appear to be the team that is failing without anybody seeming to notice.

At Stamford Bridge, the environment is conducive to Alonso and his team doing well this season.

Chelsea – not in Europe after last season's troubles – are only playing once a week. So Alonso – hired for his coaching reputation – has time on the grass with players who should arrive every weekend with freshness in their legs.

It's the environment that enabled Michael Carrick to fool everyone at Manchester United last season. While the rest of the Premier League got bogged down in the schedule, United sailed upwards on the back of a lighter load.

When we look at Alonso's team we see only familiar Chelsea things – and not in a good way.

Inconsistent tactics, some strange selections and, on the back of it, some very ordinary results.

This is the cycle Alonso was hired to break and he is not yet succeeding.

Sunday's defeat to Sunderland can be added to league setbacks against Spurs, Brentford and Arsenal.

They were unimpressive in beating United a couple of weeks ago also. Carrick's team outplayed them in the first half and should have been two or three goals ahead.

Under Alonso, Chelsea are yet to establish an identity or discernible patterns. It is hard to know yet what his best back four (or five) looks like. In the absence of the injured striker Joao Pedro, Alonso seems happier to play without one rather than use Danny Welbeck, signed for just this scenario in the summer.

The absence of Joao Pedro is significant while Alonso is also without his first choice goalkeeper Emi Martinez. These things matter.

But Chelsea have a huge squad of international players. Maybe it's too big. Whatever the case Alonso must get the best out of it soon.

Nobody seems to be talking about how very underwhelming the whole thing feels. But if it continues, they soon will be.

On Match of the Day on Sunday night, football's most vanilla pundit Dion Dublin was asked whether Michael Carrick has done enough to keep his job.

'I think so,' said Dublin. 'I think Michael has all the tools but the players just aren't doing what they need to do.'

At every other club in the Premier League, under-performing players and the bad results that tend to follow lead to intense scrutiny and criticism of the manager. It's his job to affect these things.

Not at United, though, where the level of public and media support for Carrick remains extraordinary and illogical.

If we applied this level of leeway to everybody else then nobody would ever be sacked.

Dion Dublin, pictured on Homes Under The Hammer duty, gave Michael Carrick an easy ride

Carrick is out of his depth at sinking Manchester United - his team are a shambles

Yes, there are a number of factors at play at Old Trafford. Yes, we know what they are and who is to blame for them. Yes, it's a very difficult job.

But the truth is that Carrick is failing in a quite spectacular fashion.

Of all the managers to have followed Sir Alex Ferguson over the last 13 and a half years, Erik ten Hag was the one who looked most out of his depth in terms of the chaotic nature of his team's football.

Carrick is now on the way to eclipsing that. His team are a shambles and that's on him. Once again, this is a mediocre league and it's quite criminal that Carrick has his group of players in the bottom three.

The former Middlesbrough manager is so out of his depth it's quite painful to watch.

It was another extraordinary afternoon at Old Trafford as United drew 4-4 with Aston Villa.

Unai Emery's Villa team is going through yet another regeneration after the sale of big-name players in the summer and balancing the Champions League with domestic football will once again be a challenge.

Emery seems to have made his mind up about one of his squad members, though, after former United and Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho was left out of the squad entirely yesterday.

Garnacho is a talented player but has made only 14 Premier League starts – and none at Villa – since leaving Old Trafford for Chelsea in the summer of 2025.

The Argentine is still only 22 so time is on his side but at some point he is going to have to do something on the field to justify the investment in a career that is currently going nowhere.

Alejandro Garnacho was left out of the squad entirely yesterday by Aston Villa

Sky's excellent touchline reporter Patrick Davison had his work cut out post-match at Old Trafford as he interviewed one manager in danger of the sack and another who had just flounced down the tunnel like a chap with his pants on fire.

Neither Michael Carrick nor Unai Emery seemed particularly comfortable in the face of Davison's questions and that's exactly as it should be.

He is there to ask questions on behalf of a broadcaster that ploughs billions of pounds into our national sport each year. He is not there to apply soothing balm.

There would appear to be many others happy to do that anyway.

Sky's Patrick Davison (right) is not there to apply soothing balm with his questions

Less impressive was the appearance of Sky's latest metric that appeared on screen during Nottingham Forest's dismantling of Manchester City on Saturday.

Titled simply 'pressures' it indicated that Forest were doing rather better at it than City.

But what did it mean? Does anybody know? Or indeed care?

Two seasons ago at the City Ground I saw local boy Ryan Yates give Casemiro such a chasing as Forest beat Manchester United that the great Brazilian was taken off before he was sent off.

On Saturday by the river, Yates made his first league start of the season as Oliver Glasner’s team overwhelmed City.

Beforehand Yates gave an address to his team-mates. He told them about what it meant to play for the club and touched briefly on its history.

He told me once in an interview that he tends to tell all new arrivals at Forest what the two stars on the shirt actually mean – two European Cups won in 1979 and 1980.

It’s smart work by a lad who knows what football means in Nottingham and it was smart work by his manager who knew that his team needed an injection of something visceral to drag him from a trough of failure that was threatening to cost him his job.

Manchester United could probably do with a bit of that right now. So, possibly, could Chelsea and indeed Tottenham. At Liverpool, they lament the absence from the team of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones.

It takes an awful lot to make up a Premier League team these days. Place of birth is not a priority any more and that’s understandable. But sometimes it helps.

When was the last time an English team won the title with a poor goalkeeper?

Flick back over the last couple of decades and it's hard to find an example.

So what hope for Manchester City this season?

Gianluigi Donnarumma is anything but a poor goalkeeper but the problem is that he is playing like one and it is there that City's current problems start.

Enzo Maresca's back four looks shot to pieces and that often happens when they lose faith in the chap behind them.

Maresca says he won't change. 'My team is Gigi plus ten others,' is his take.

Enzo Maresca says he will not change goalkeeper despite Gianluigi Donnarumma's problems

His back up is 34-year-old Argentinean Geronimo Rulli, a member of his country's World Cup squad with nine caps to his name.

Rulli is well-travelled and has some pedigree. He was, for example, Villarreal's hero as they beat Manchester United in a Europa League final shoot out in 2021.

If Maresca trusts him then maybe now is the time to show it. If he doesn't then why did City sign him?

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is perhaps not quite what he once was at the age of 34 but produced a throwback performance for his team at Crystal Palace. Without him, Liverpool would not have won.

Nevertheless Palace's struggles go on and their coach Pierre Sage is in danger of losing his job.

However the south London club cannot say they were not warned about trouble ahead.

Former manager Oliver Glasner spent most of last season in a huff about what he saw as a failure by the Palace board to invest properly in the squad.

Palace have won twice in ten Premier League games this season and it seems Glasner may have been right.

Brighton continue to fly high and to produce such an energetic performance to beat Brentford having played away at Getafe in Europe on Thursday was testimony to the fitness of Fabian Hurzeler's squad.

The Seagulls were certainly helped by having to play against ten for an hour, though, and on Match of the Day the enduringly listenable Jonathan Pearce spoke for all of us as he watched Chema Andres go down after minimal contact to his cheek from Brentford's Igor Thiago.

'That was nothing, nothing, nothing,' said Pearce as Thiago walked off.

Coming so soon after theatrics from Alexis MacAllister and Gabriel in the Liverpool-Arsenal game last week, the issue of players exaggerating facial contact to get opponents sent off remains a live one.

Brentford's manager Keith Andrews was measured on the issue but suggested the tactic was becoming 'a game within a game'.

It's a problem and referees head Howard Webb needs his officials to get a grip of it.

Brighton's Pascal Gross has now created more than 25 chances for team-mates this season and that's more than anyone else in the Premier League.

Gross cost £1.2million when he returned to the club from Borussia Dortmund last January.

It constitutes another steal in the market by Brighton's stat boffins but this time they probably didn't need the data to convince them of its merits.

Pascal Gross scored on Sunday and has now created more than 25 chances for team-mates

Bournemouth, meanwhile, cast their net as widely as anybody these days and that includes all the way down the English pyramid.

The South Coast club – on an eight-match winning streak now under Marco Rose – have a relationship with yesterday's FA Cup giant killers Wimborne from the seventh tier.

Wimborne of the Southern League Premier South beat League Two Crawley in Round One and will this week send their Chilean teenage striker Angel Diaz for a trial at the Premier League club.

Story of last season in the EFL was probably Lincoln City's promotion to the Championship where, after 15 games, they are just about keeping their heads above water in 21st place.

Architect of that incredible rise was former futsal coach Michael Skubala who rather sullied the romantic feel of it all by quitting almost immediately to join Bristol City.

This weekend Skubala's team were thrashed 5-0 at home by Norwich with the home fans singing that their manager would be 'sacked in the morning'.

Lincoln have already won at Ashton Gate, back in September, at the start of a run that has seen City win just two from ten.

Sometimes, it really does pay just to stay where you are.

#1640. Michael Carrick: Man United's worst starts to a Premier League season and where the ex-England international ranks

By Joshua Cole | 12 Nov 2026 16:37

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick following their worst start to a Premier League season, with the former midfielder paying the price for a disastrous opening to the 2026-27 campaign.

The Red Devils were expected to build on last season's encouraging third-place finish after Carrick guided them back into the Champions League, but their performances have deteriorated dramatically since the summer.

Sunday's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa proved the final straw for the club's hierarchy, with United having collected just eight points from their opening 10 league matches to leave them 18th in the table.

Their solitary victory during that period represents a particularly concerning statistic for a club of their stature, especially considering that they had finished the previous campaign among the Premier League's top three.

Carrick's dismissal has therefore brought renewed attention to the club's historical struggles, with the 2026-27 campaign now ranking as their worst opening to a Premier League season after nine matches.

While United have endured difficult starts in previous campaigns, their current situation is particularly alarming given the resources available to the club and their expectations of competing for Champions League qualification.

Here, Sports Mole looks at Manchester United's five worst starts to a Premier League season, examining the results, circumstances and eventual outcomes of those campaigns.

Manchester United's current campaign sits at the bottom of this unwanted ranking, with Carrick's team collecting just seven points from their opening nine Premier League matches before the situation deteriorated further against Aston Villa.

Their only victory during that period came against Ipswich Town, while draws against Everton, Fulham, Tottenham and Leeds exposed their inability to turn promising situations into maximum points.

Defeats against Hull City, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Chelsea further increased the pressure on Carrick, whose team struggled to establish any consistency in their performances.

The 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham was particularly frustrating, while their inability to secure three points against Aston Villa despite scoring four goals demonstrated the defensive problems that had undermined their campaign.

United eventually reached 10 matches with eight points, leaving them 18th in the table and prompting the hierarchy to dismiss Carrick on November 12.

According to Opta Analyst, this is their worst start to a Premier League season, with the previous lowest return being 10 points after nine matches in 2019-20.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer endured a difficult opening to his first full season as Manchester United manager, with the Norwegian struggling to build on the optimism generated during his initial caretaker spell.

United collected only 10 points from their first nine Premier League matches, winning two, drawing four and losing three, with their problems in front of goal becoming increasingly apparent.

Their campaign included disappointing draws against Wolverhampton Wanderers, Southampton and West Ham United, while a 2-0 defeat against West Ham at the London Stadium left Solskjaer facing growing criticism.

A 1-1 draw against Liverpool at Old Trafford on October 20 offered some encouragement, although United subsequently lost against Bournemouth before returning to winning ways against Norwich City.

Solskjaer ultimately survived the difficult opening and guided United to a third-place finish, collecting 66 points from 38 matches and securing Champions League qualification.

Erik ten Hag's third season at Old Trafford began disappointingly, with Manchester United collecting just 11 points from their opening nine Premier League fixtures.

The Red Devils won three, drew two and lost four of those matches, with their performances raising serious questions about Ten Hag's ability to deliver consistent improvement.

A 3-0 home defeat against Liverpool in September was particularly damaging, while subsequent losses against Tottenham and West Ham United increased the pressure on the Dutchman.

United also struggled to score consistently, with their attacking approach lacking the organisation and effectiveness required to compete with the leading sides.

The 2-1 defeat against West Ham on October 27 proved to be Ten Hag's final match, with the club dismissing him the following day.

He departed with United sitting 14th in the table, having collected just 11 points from nine matches, and was replaced by Sporting Lisbon manager Ruben Amorim.

David Moyes's successor, Louis van Gaal, also experienced a difficult introduction to life at Manchester United, with the Dutchman taking over following the club's disastrous seventh-place finish under the Scot.

Despite arriving with an impressive managerial reputation and having guided the Netherlands to the World Cup semi-finals in Brazil, Van Gaal struggled to establish consistency during his first few months.

United won three, drew four and lost two of their opening nine Premier League matches, collecting 13 points as their defensive problems continued from the previous campaign.

A 5-3 defeat against Leicester City in September was particularly damaging, with United surrendering a two-goal advantage against the newly promoted Foxes.

However, Van Gaal gradually improved the team's performances, with victories against Crystal Palace, Arsenal and Liverpool helping them secure fourth place with 70 points.

Although his first season was far from convincing, he restored Champions League football before eventually being dismissed in May 2016, shortly after winning the FA Cup.

Ten Hag's second season at Manchester United also began with considerable difficulties, despite the Dutchman having guided the club to a third-place finish and Carabao Cup success during his first campaign.

United won five and lost four of their opening nine Premier League matches, collecting 15 points, with their performances suggesting that the progress made previously had begun to stall.

A 3-1 defeat against Arsenal was followed by losses against Brighton and Bayern Munich, while a 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City further exposed the gap between United and the Premier League's leading teams.

Although they subsequently recovered to finish eighth with 60 points, their lowest Premier League position at the time, Ten Hag's future remained uncertain.

He was eventually dismissed in October 2024 following another disappointing opening to the following campaign, with the club deciding that a change was necessary after failing to see sufficient progress.

#1639. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

Our team to take on Leeds United 🙌Watch the game LIVE on All Red Video:

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. #1638. Next Man Utd manager: Mauricio Pochettino timeline 'revealed' with two-game delay possible

By Carter White | 12 Nov 2026 16:40

Manchester United have reportedly agreed to wait until next week to have Mauricio Pochettino at their Carrington training base.

The Red Devils are on the hunt for a new first-team head coach following the dismissal of Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, with the 20-time English champions sitting 18th in the Premier League standings.

Man Utd have managed to win just one of their opening 10 top-flight contests, with that sole success coming at Old Trafford against newly-promoted Ipswich Town at the end of the summer.

With the managerial position now vacant at the Theatre of Dreams, USA coach Pochettino has emerged as the favourite to take the reins, with the Argentine heading towards a return to the Premier League.

The 54-year-old has managed both Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the past, taking the former London club to the Champions League final in 2019, when they lost to Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool.

The process of appointing Pochettino is not straightforward, with the Argentine currently in position as the head coach of the United States, who have a two-legged quarter-final with Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League over the next week.

As per ESPN, Manchester United are confident of agreeing personal terms with their top managerial target before the close of play on Thursday (November 12), after which point they will trigger the release clause in the coach's contract.

The report claims that the Red Devils will need to fork out £7m to take Pochettino away from the Stars and Stripes, with the 54-year-old's representatives supposedly contacting the Premier League giants to make them aware of the clause.

Surprisingly, Man Utd are said to be relaxed about the former Spurs boss staying in post with the United States for their double-header against Haiti, with the second leg taking place late on Tuesday night.

As a result, Pochettino is likely to arrive at the Red Devils' Carrington training base on next Wednesday (November 18) - just a few days before a crunch Premier League clash at Liverpool on November 22.

There is seemingly a chance that Pochettino takes charge of the United States twice more before departing to Manchester United, who are in danger of a relegation dogfight this season.

Whilst the Red Devils will be keen to have the Argentine in England as quickly as possible, there is also a realisation that the majority of the club's senior stars are currently away on international duty.

By the time Pochettino arrives at Carrington next Wednesday, most of Man United's first team players will have finished their national matches, focused on turning around the fortunes of England's grandest club.

#1636. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. #1635. Man Utd legend brands Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada conduct 'disgusting' following classless Michael Carrick dismissal

By Carter White | 12 Nov 2026 17:13

Manchester United legend Gary Neville has criticised the club's treatment of outgoing head coach Michael Carrick.

With the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table, the decision has been made to part ways with their former midfielder, who took charge of first-team matters from Ruben Amorim in January.

United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the clear favourite to take the reins at Old Trafford, with Man Utd supposedly reaching an agreement in principle for the former Tottenham Hotspur boss.

That being said, it is understood that the 54-year-old could still be in the dugout for the Stars and Stripes as they face Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League over the next few days.

The highlight of Pochettino's career in England was undoubtedly taking Spurs to the Champions League final in 2019, with the Lilywhites eventually losing to Mohamed Salah, Jurgen Klopp and Liverpool.

Speaking to Sky Sports News, ex-Manchester United defender Neville has branded the club's treatment of Carrick as "disgusting", insisting that the Red Devils have gone about their latest managerial dismissal in the wrong way.

"In the last 24-48 hours it has been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive (Omar Berrada) and an owner (Sir Jim Ratcliffe) whilst your manager, who is a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach  Pochettino," said Neville.

"It is just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you would be getting sued.

"The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it is just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership. I do not think anybody comes out of this well at all."

Carrick was relieved of his Man Utd duties after winning just three of 15 competitive matches at the beginning of the 2026-27 season, with the club in danger of experiencing a relegation battle this term.

As alluded to by Neville, Manchester United CEO Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox visited co-owner Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday (November 11) to discuss the future of Carrick.

Wilcox and Berrada both advised the Red Devils' owner that the best course of action would be to dismiss the legendary midfielder after the club's worst start to a Premier League season in 40 years.

Whilst these meetings were taking place in Monte Carlo, Carrick remained at base and in position on the Carrington training pitches, coaching the first-teamers who are not involved on the international scene over the next week.
